articles.title: Email Notifications
articles.body:
PensionPro can provide a firm's Employees and Contacts with notifications via email to alert them of various actions taken in PensionPro. For example, an Employee might be notified when a Task or To-Do is assigned to them, and a Contact might be notified if their email address is updated. This article discusses the types of notifications that may be sent, the preferences for these notifications, and how Employees can customize the types of notifications they receive.

 

Tier Availability: Team, Business

 

 

 Note: Some items may not be available in all tiers.
 

 

 

Article Contents

 

 - Types of Email Notifications

 - Personal Notification Settings

 - Firm Notification Preferences

 - Frequently Asked Questions

 

 

Types of Email Notifications

 

The following types of notifications may either be customized or enabled/disabled as desired:

 

 - Alerts when items such as To-Dos or Proposals are assigned to an Employee

 - Alerts when Tasks are assigned to or become active for an Employee, or one of the Employee's Worktrays

 - Notifications that a Plan Sponsor performed an action on PlanSponsorLink

 - Notifications to a Contact that their email address on file was updated

 

PensionPro provides a number of other system notifications that cannot be customized, such as temporary password emails and queuing confirmations for Import Power Tools. These notifications will not be covered in this article.

 

 

 Note: Actions performed in bulk using Power Tools or
 other
 functionality will generate a single notification containing the applicable
 number of items.
 

 

 

 Note: Notification emails are not sent if the individual
 performing the action that generates a notification is the same individual
 who would receive it.
 

 

 

 

Personal Notification Settings

 

Employees can customize which notifications they receive regarding items that are assigned to them, such as Tasks. These notifications will alert the Employee to new PensionPro activity, even when they are not currently using the application.

 

To manage personal notification preferences:

 

 - In the PensionPro header at the top-right, select More > View My Account. A new Employee tab opens.

 - Expand the Preferences category from the Views list on the left, then select Email Notification. The corresponding grid displays.

 - Hover over any preference in the grid, then select Edit on the right to open the Edit Preference window.

 

 

 Note: If the Email Notification view is not available
 in
 the Views list, then the firm has not enabled notifications. Likewise,
 if
 each preference in the Email Notifications grid is set to
 Controlled By Firm, the firm is managing notification settings
 globally
 for all users. In either case, no personalization is available. For more
 information, refer to the section
 Firm Notification Preferences.
 

 

 

The user preferences available in the Email Notification grid are as follows:

 

 | Enable User Email Notifications
 | 

Determines whether the user receives email notifications.

 - Setting this value to No has no effect on required system communications, nor does it affect notifications that are controlled elsewhere.

 | Proposal Assignment Email Notification
 | If Yes, a notification is sent when a Proposal is assigned to the user.

 | Prospect Assignment Email Notification
 | If Yes, a notification is sent when a Prospect is assigned to the user.

 | Secure File Exchange Accessed Email Notification
 | If Yes, a notification is sent when a Secure File Exchange sent to the user is accessed by another Employee.

 | Task Activation Email Notification
 | If Yes, a notification is sent when a Task that is currently assigned to the user becomes active.

 | Task Reassignment Email Notification
 | If Yes, a notification is sent when an active Task is reassigned to the user.

 | To-Do Reassignment Email Notification
 | If Yes, a notification is sent when a To-Do is assigned to the user.

 | Worktray Reassignment Email Notification
 | If Yes, a notification is sent when an active Task is reassigned to one of the user's Worktrays.

 | Worktray Task Activation Email Notification
 | If Yes, a notification is sent when a Task currently assigned to one of the user's Worktrays becomes active.

User email notification preferences
 

 

 

Firm Notification Preferences

 

Notification emails can be controlled on a firm-wide level. In addition to the Employee alerts discussed in the section Personal Notification Settings, PensionPro provides more detailed control over a notification's content and recipient in certain cases.

 

 Requires Security Rights: Maintenance
 

 

To manage the firm's notification preferences:

 

 - Select Maintenance > Preferences > PensionPro. The PensionPro Preference Maintenance tab opens.

 - Expand the General category from the Views list on the left, then select Notifications. The corresponding grid displays.

 - Hover over any preference in the grid, then select Edit on the right to open the Edit Preference window.

 

The available notification preferences are shown below; they have been grouped based on their functions:

 

 | Enable Email Notifications
 | 

This setting enables or disables all email notifications across PensionPro.

 - Setting this value to No has no effect on required system communications.

 | Enable User Control
 | 

When enabled, users can turn various assignment notification emails on/off on an individual basis within their account preferences. If disabled, these emails are turned on/off globally.

 - If this option is set to Yes, the below preferences will be set to Controlled by User and cannot be edited globally.

 - This option is not applicable if Enable Email Notifications is set to No.

 | Proposal Assignment Email Notification
 | Determines whether a user will receive an email when a Proposal is assigned to them.

 | Prospect Assignment Email Notification
 | Determines whether a user will receive an email when a Prospect is assigned to them.

 | Secure File Exchange Accessed Email Notification
 | Determines whether a user who received a Secure File Exchange from a Contact will receive an email if another Employee accesses the file.

 | Task Activation Email Notification
 | Determines whether a user will receive an email when a Task assigned to them becomes active.

 | Task Reassignment Email Notification
 | Determines whether a user will receive an email when a Task is reassigned to them.

 | To-Do Reassignment Email Notification
 | Determines whether a user will receive an email when a To-Do item is reassigned to them.

 | Worktray Reassignment Email Notification
 | Determines whether a Worktray's users will receive an email when a Task is reassigned to that Worktray.

 | Worktray Task Activation Email Notification
 | Determines whether a Worktray's users will receive an email when a Task assigned to that Worktray becomes active.

Firm-wide email notification preferences
 

 

 | Annual Administration Document Upload Recipient Email
 | The email address where notification is sent. This static address will be used if Annual Administration Document Upload Recipient Role is blank or specifies an Employee Role that is not assigned for the relevant Plan.

 | Annual Administration Document Upload Recipient Role
 | If set, the notification email will be sent to the Employee assigned to this Plan Role for the relevant Plan. May be left blank.

These preferences apply to the notification email that is sent when a file is uploaded during the Approval step of Annual Data Collection
 

 

 | ATC Payment Response Recipient Email
 | The email address where notification is sent. This static address will be used if ATC Payment Response Recipient Role is blank or specifies an Employee Role that is not assigned for the relevant Plan.

 | ATC Payment Response Recipient Role
 | If set, the notification email will be sent to the Employee assigned to this Plan Role for the relevant Plan. May be left blank.

These preferences apply to the notification emails sent regarding status updates when using the ATC Paying Agent Integration for Distributions
 

 

 | Contact Change Request Recipient Email
 | The email address where the notification is sent. This static address will be used if Contact Change Request Recipient Role is blank or specifies an Employee Role that is not assigned for the relevant Plan.

 | Contact Change Request Recipient Role
 | If set, the notification email will be sent to the Employee assigned to this Plan Role for the relevant Plan. May be left blank.

These preferences apply to the notification email that is sent to the TPA when the Plan Sponsor requests changes to Plan Contact Roles on PlanSponsorLink
 

 

 | Contact Email Notification Subject to Existing Email
 | The subject line of the notification email sent to the Contact's previous email address.

 | Contact Email Notification Subject to Updated Email
 | The subject line of the notification email sent to the Contact's new email address.

 | Contact Email Notification to Existing Email
 | The body of the notification email sent to the Contact's previous email address.

 | Contact Email Notification to Updated Email
 | The body of the notification email sent to the Contact's new email address.

 | Enable Email Address Notification Change
 | When enabled, updating a Contact's email address will send a notification email to the previous and new addresses. If disabled, no notifications are sent.

These preferences apply to the notification emails that are sent to a Contact when their email address is changed in PensionPro
 

 

 | Deactivated Plan Data Available For Download Email CC
 | The email address where the notification is CC'd; the user who deactivated the Plan will be the primary recipient.

This preference applies to the notification email that is sent after a Plan is deactivated, when its backup data becomes available for export
 

 

 | Distribution Document Upload Recipient Email
 | The email address where notification is sent. This static address will be used if Distribution Document Upload Recipient Role is blank or specifies an Employee Role that is not assigned for the relevant Plan.

 | Distribution Document Upload Recipient Role
 | If set, the notification email will be sent to the Employee assigned to this Plan Role for the relevant Plan. May be left blank.

These preferences apply to the notification email that is sent when a file is uploaded to a Distribution via the Distribution tab on PlanSponsorLink
 

 

 | Fiduciary Document Upload Recipient Email Address
 | The email address where the notification is sent. This static address will be used if Fiduciary Document Upload Recipient Role is blank or specifies an Employee Role that is not assigned for the relevant Plan.

 | Fiduciary Document Upload Recipient Role
 | If set, the notification email will be sent to the Employee assigned to this Plan Role for the relevant Plan. May be left blank.

These preferences apply to the notification email that is sent to the TPA when the Plan Sponsor uploads a Fiduciary Document on PlanSponsorLink
 

 

 | Project Document Upload Recipient Email
 | The email address where notification is sent. This static address will be used if Project Document Upload Recipient Role is blank or specifies an Employee Role that is not assigned for a relevant Plan.

 | Project Document Upload Recipient Role
 | 

If set, the notification email will be sent to the Employee assigned to this Plan Role for a relevant Plan. May be left blank.

 - In this case, "relevant Plans" include any Plans belonging to the Client associated with the payroll file. This notification may be received by multiple Employees.

These preferences apply to the notification email that is sent to the TPA when a new file lands on the Payroll Dashboard from an integrated payroll service.
 

 

 | Project Document Upload Recipient Email
 | The email address where notification is sent. This static address will be used if Project Document Upload Recipient Role is blank or specifies an Employee Role that is not assigned for the relevant Plan.

 | Project Document Upload Recipient Role
 | If set, the notification email will be sent to the Employee assigned to this Plan Role for the relevant Plan. May be left blank.

These preferences apply to the notification email that is sent when a file is uploaded to a Project via the Project tab on PlanSponsorLink
 

 

 

 Note: Some notification emails—such as those alerting
 the
 TPA of an address change made on PlanSponsorLink—have settings that reside
 in more relevant locations (such as the
 Annual Data Collection view in the above case). Refer
 to
 the articles
 PensionPro Preferences
 and PlanSponsorLink Preferences
 for more details.
 

 

 

 

Frequently Asked Questions

 

 - 
Is an Interaction created for each email notification?
No; email notifications do not create an Interaction.
 

 - 
If I override a Task, is a notification email still sent to the Employee assigned to the Task that directly follows it?
Yes, the Employee will be notified that the Task has become active as normal.
 

 - 
If I return a Task, is a notification email still sent to the Employee that originally performed the work?
Yes, the Employee will be notified that an assigned Task has been activated.
 

 - 
I'm not receiving a notification email when I perform certain actions in PensionPro or PlanSponsorLink. Why?
PensionPro does not generate an email in cases where a notification is expected to not be necessary; for example, an Employee activating a Task assigned to themself. In PSL, this suppression is limited to actions performed by Employee accounts, such as an Employee submitting a Contact Change Request. Actions performed by Contacts will always generate an email where expected.

articles.title: Files & Documents
articles.body:
Reports, forms, and other documents are an important part of plan administration—both for keeping internal records, and for sharing information with a client. PensionPro provides document storage in the form of Files for Plans, Projects, and Plan Cycles; once uploaded, these Files can be easily distributed to Plan Contacts via PlanSponsorLink.

 

Tier Availability: Team, Business

 

 

 Note: Some items may not be available in all tiers.
 

 

Article Contents

 

 - 
Where Files are Used
 - Plan Files

 - Project Files

 - Plan Cycle Files

 - Other Files

 - Understanding File Types

 - 
Working with Files
 - Adding, Editing, & Deleting Files

 - Downloading Files & Access Logs

 - Archiving Files

 - Combining Files

 - Sending Files to DocuSign

 - 
Files on PlanSponsorLink
 - Website Rights for Files

 - Adding Files in PlanSponsorLink

 - Frequently Asked Questions

 

 

Where Files are Used

 

Files can be added to a variety of different records in PensionPro. Some functionality may differ depending on the type of record that the File is uploaded to; as such, it is important to understand the record types available, and which functions apply to each.

 

 

Plan Files

 

Uploading a File to a Plan is the most common method of adding a File to PensionPro. Due to the large number of documents that may be involved, Plan Files are broken up into three categories:

 

 - 
Legal Plan Files: Legal documents, such as Safe Harbor Notices and Valuation Reports.

 - 
Administrative Files: Forms used in general Plan administration, such as a Beneficiary Form, Hardship Form, or Withdrawal Form.

 - 
Fiduciary Files: Documents connected to fiduciary responsibilities, including Fiduciary Minutes, Fund Performance Reports, and Portfolio Performance Reports. 

 

Plan Files are found on the corresponding Plan tab; each of the above categories has a dedicated view, found under the Files view grouping on the left. A Plan File may be posted to PlanSponsorLink and maintains an Access Log; it may also be sent to DocuSign as an E-Signature Document.

 

 

Project Files

 

Tier Availability: Business

 

Files may also be added to individual Projects, although these are not broken up into additional categories like Plan Files are. Instead, all of a Project's Files are accessible from the Files view of the Project tab.

 

Like Plan Files, Project Files may be posted to PlanSponsorLink, maintain Access Logs, and may be sent to DocuSign as an E-Signature Document.

 

Distribution Files function similarly to Project Files.

 

 

Plan Cycle Files

 

Tier Availability: Team

 

On PensionPro's Team tier, Files may be added to each yearly Plan Cycle record. All of a Plan Cycle's Files are accessible from the Files view of the Plan Cycle tab.

 

Plan Cycle Files may be posted to PlanSponsorLink and maintain Access Logs.

 

 

Other Files

 

In addition to the above, Files may also be added to other areas of PensionPro, such as the following:

 

 - Record types added by SalesPitch, such as Proposals

 - Collection Items for General Web Collection

 - 
Blast Email attachments

 - Bulletins on PlanSponsorLink

 

The instructions for managing Files found in the remainder of this article are generally applicable to these areas, but there may be some differences. Additionally, some functionalities may not be available for these Files. For specific instructions, refer to the appropriate article.

 

 

Understanding File Types

 

Plan and Project Files require a File Type be assigned to them before they can be added. The File Type helps further categorize a File and offers additional options for organization. File Types may be different depending on where the File is being added; for example, File Types for Plans might differ from those added to Projects.

 

Managing File Types

 

 Requires Security Rights: Maintenance
 

 

File Types are managed as List Values, located within List Value Maintenance under Core > File Types. The following list notes where each each File Type is used:

 

 - 
Administrative Form Type: Plan Files > Administrative Forms

 - 
Distribution: Distribution Files

 - 
Fiduciary: Plan Files > Fiduciary Files

 - 
Plan Document: Plan Files > Legal Plan Files

 - 
Project: Project Files

 

The Document Collection File Type is deprecated and no longer used.

 

 

Working with Files

 

The instructions in the following sections pertain specifically to managing Plan, Project, and Plan Cycle Files. Files may be added and removed, archived, downloaded, and more from their respective views on the Plan, Project, or Plan Cycle tab.

 

 

Adding, Editing, & Deleting Files

 

To upload a new file to PensionPro:

 

 - Select Add at the top-right of the Files grid. The corresponding Add File window displays.

 - Use the File Selection box to navigate to and select the desired file using the file explorer.

 - Enter a Title for the File.

 - Select the File's Type; refer to the section File Types for more information.

 - Select a PSL Category for the File. - This option is required even if the file will not be shown on PlanSponsorLink.

 - (optional) Add a Description or Effective Date.

 - (optional) Select Show on PSL to make the File available for Plan Contacts on PlanSponsorLink. Refer to the section Files on PlanSponsorLink for more information.

 - (optional) Select Send E-Signature Document to send the file to DocuSign after it is added. Refer to the section Sending a File to DocuSign of the article DocuSign Integration for more information.

 - When finished, select Save. The File will be uploaded and added to the Plan or Project.

 

Files must not be larger than 1 GB, and may not have any of the following extensions: .exe, .cmd, .bat, and .msi.

 

Hovering over a File in the grid will display the Edit and Delete options on the right-hand side. The File's details may be edited, but the actual uploaded file cannot be changed; it must be archived/deleted and re-uploaded.

 

Deleting a File directly requires the Delete Documents Security Right; a user without this Security Right may instead edit the File and select Mark for Deletion to add it to the Data Deletion Manager.

 

 

Downloading Files & Access Logs

 

To download any File uploaded to PensionPro, double-click it in the grid; alternately, click it once in the grid to select it, then select More > Download.

 

Once a File is downloaded by any user, it will be considered Accessed. An Access Date will populate for the File, and the user's name will be added to the Access Log along with a timestamp.

 

To review an Access Log, select View Access Log in the grid, to the right of the File's Title. The Access Log records all users who downloaded the File; if the File was posted to PlanSponsorLink, this also includes any Plan Sponsors who accessed it.

 

If necessary, an Access Log can be cleared, indicating that the File has not been accessed until the next time it is downloaded. To do so, Edit the File and clear the Mark as Accessed field.

 

 

Archiving Files

 

When a File is archived, it remains in PensionPro, but it is hidden from the Files grid by default. Archiving a File may be preferable to deleting it in some cases.

 

To archive a File, select Edit on the right, then select Archived. Once saved, the File will be hidden from the grid.

 

To view archived Files in the grid, select More > Show Archived. Repeating this action will provide the Hide Archived option instead.

 

 

Combining Files

 

Occasionally, it makes sense to combine multiple different documents into a single file, such as when compiling an annual participant notice. PensionPro can do this easily without the use of any additional tools.

 

The ability to combine Files is only available on the Plan tab. PensionPro can only combine Files that have already been added to the Plan; new Files cannot be uploaded during this process. Files with different extensions can be combined freely; refer to the below chart for acceptable file types.

 

Can be combined
Result can be saved as

 | 
 - Document: .doc, .docx, .pdf, .odt, .rtf, .txt

 - Spreadsheet: .xls, .xlsx, .csv

 - Markup: .html, .xml

 - Image: .jpg, .jpeg, .png

 | 
 - Document: .docx, .pdf, .odt, .rtf, .txt

 - Markup: .html, .xml

Supported extensions for combining Files
 

 

 Note: PensionPro recommends using .docx or .pdf for created
 Files. File type conversion may result in unexpected formatting or lost data;
 always review combined Files following creation.
 

 

To combine multiple Plan Files:

 

 - In either the Legal Plan Files, Administrative Forms, or Fiduciary Files grid, Ctrl-click to select up to 5 Files.

 - Select More > Combine Files. The corresponding window displays.

 - The chosen Files are listed at the top of the Combine Files window. Drag Files up and down in this list to set their order in the combined document. - Files cannot be added to or removed from this list. To change which Files will be included, close the Combine Files window and return to Step 1.

 - Choose the desired File Format and set the Title of the new file.

 - Complete the remaining fields for setting File details. These are similar to those found in the section Adding, Editing, & Deleting Files.

 - (optional) Select Archive Original Files to hide the incorporated documents from the Files grid; refer to the section Archiving Files.

 - Select Save.

 

Upon creation, the combined document will be added to the Files grid and can be used like any other File.

 

 

Sending Files to DocuSign

 

If PensionPro's DocuSign integration is properly established and E-Signature Templates have been created, a Plan or Project File may be sent to DocuSign for electronic signature. For instructions, refer to the Sending a File to DocuSign section of the article DocuSign Integration.

 

 

Retrieving ftwilliam.com Files

 

If the integration with ftwilliam.com is in use and the Plan is properly linked, a selection of plan-specific documents can be easily downloaded to Legal Plan Files. More information about this functionality can be found in the article ftwilliam.com - Document Download.

 

 

Files on PlanSponsorLink

 

Plan, Project, and Plan Cycle Files may optionally be posted to PlanSponsorLink to be viewed and downloaded by Plan Contacts. This gives Contacts the ability to access Plan documents at any time.

 

To post a File to PlanSponsorLink, select the Show on PSL option when adding or editing the File.

 

 

 Note: If desired, once a File is marked to be shown on PSL
 and then saved, PensionPro can open an email draft in the user's default
 email application. This draft will include a prefilled subject and body to
 quickly notify Plan Sponsors that a new File is available. To utilize this
 functionality, enable Document Email Use within PensionPro
 Document Preferences. For more information, refer to the
 Documents section of the article
 PensionPro Preferences.
 

 

A File posted to PSL will be available in the Plan Sponsor's My Active Tasks tab until they download the File for the first time. Once downloaded, the File will disappear from My Active Tasks, but will remain available on the Plan Sponsor's Documents tab. PensionPro and PlanSponsorLink users who upload a File will not see it in their own My Active Tasks tab.

 

Plan Administrative Forms are not displayed on the My Active Tasks tab, but are available on the Documents tab.

 

Regardless of whether Show On PSL is selected, PensionPro will require a PSL Category be set. These categories group together similar Files for PlanSponsorLink users on the Documents tab. Files given the same category will be grouped together in PSL, even if they were uploaded to different areas of PensionPro (such as the Plan and Project tabs). Category names are managed as List Values, located within List Value Maintenance under Core > File Types > Web Category. 

 

 

Website Rights for Files

 

To view Files on PlanSponsorLink, a user must be assigned appropriate Website Rights for each Plan they are assigned to as a Plan Contact Role. A number of Website Rights exist, each allowing a Plan Sponsor to view a certain category of file; for example, Website Rights determine whether the Plan Sponsor can view Legal or Fiduciary Files. Refer to the Website Rights for Plan Contacts section of the article Managing PlanSponsorLink Users.

 

 

Adding Files from PlanSponsorLink

 

Plan Sponsors have the ability to upload Files directly to a Plan, Project, or Plan Cycle within PlanSponsorLink. This functionality is available in the following areas:

 

Documents tab

 

 Requires Website Rights: Add/Edit/Delete Fiduciary Documents

 

Files may be added to a Plan's Fiduciary Files by selecting Upload Fiduciary Document at the top-right.

 

Projects and Distributions tabs

 

 Requires Website Rights: Projects, Distribution

 

When a Project or Distribution is available in one of these tabs, select View on the right-hand side to open the View Project or View Distribution window. Use Add in the Documents section to select a file for upload.

 

Annual Data Collection

 

 Requires Website Rights: Approval

 

A File uploaded during the Approval step of Annual Data Collection will be added to the Project (Business tier) or Plan Cycle (Team tier). Use Add in the Documents section of this step to select a file for upload.

 

 

Frequently Asked Questions

 

 - 
What options do I have for managing Files in bulk?
A File cannot be uploaded to multiple Plans, Projects, or Plan Cycles. However, once added, Files may be managed using the Files Field Update Power Tool. This Tool provides the ability to update the Archived, Marked for Deletion, and Show on PSL fields for multiple Files where applicable. Refer to the Field Update section of the article Power Tools.
 

 - 
Why isn't my File appearing on PlanSponsorLink after I just uploaded it?
A File will not appear on the My Active Tasks tab of PSL for the user who uploaded it. This helps prevent an Employee from accidentally marking the File as accessed when confirming that the File uploaded successfully to PSL. The File will still be available on the Documents tab.
 

 - 
Is there a limit to the length of time Files are retained?
No; Files are retained in PensionPro until removed by the firm.

articles.title: Interactions
articles.body:
PensionPro can store records of emails, telephone calls, appointments, and meetings with Contacts; these records are referred to as Interactions. Interactions are useful for recalling previous communications and identifying what information was conveyed, helping to maintain a "paper trail" or to determine which Clients are overdue for outreach.

 

Tier Availability: Team, Business

 

Article Contents

 

 - Overview of Interactions

 - 
Working with Interactions
 - Viewing Interaction Details

 - Editing Interactions

 - Resending or Forwarding Blast Email Interactions

 - Deleting Interactions

 - 
Adding Interactions to PensionPro
 - Manually Adding an Interaction

 - Adding an Interaction from an Email File (Drag-and-Drop)

 - Automatically-Generated Interactions

 - Customizing Interaction Types & Roles

 

 

Overview of Interactions

 

An Interaction records details of a communication, such as what type of Interaction it was, the date it occurred, and who the participants were. Depending on the Interaction type, this might also include a summary of what was discussed, or the contents of an email that was sent or received.

 

Interactions are present in many locations throughout PensionPro, and may be associated with one or more of the following record types:

 

 - 
Contacts: If an Interaction participant exists in PensionPro as a Contact, their Contact record will be linked to the Interaction.

 - 
Plans: An Interaction can be associated with a Plan, if applicable.

 - 
Clients: All Interactions across all of a Client's Plans can be viewed in one place.

 - 
Prospects, Opportunities, Proposals: SalesPitch items can be linked to Interactions similarly to Plans.

 

Because a lot of client communication can occur in a single day, PensionPro makes recording Interactions as convenient as possible. Some Interactions are generated automatically when using features such as Blast Email; others can be added quickly from Microsoft Outlook. For any other communications, adding Interactions is simple and can be done from any location in PensionPro.

 

 

Working with Interactions

 

Interactions can be viewed under many different record types throughout PensionPro. To open the Interactions grid for a record:

 

 - Open one of the record types from the table below.

 - With the record's tab open, select Interactions from the list of views.

 

Record
Includes
Notes

 | Contact
 | Interactions where the Contact is a participant
 | An Employee's Interactions are found on their corresponding Contact tab.

 | Plan
 | Interactions linked to the Plan
 |  

 | Client
 | Interactions linked to any Plan under the Client
 | Here, Interactions can only be viewed, not added or edited.

 | Prospect, Opportunity, Proposal
 | Interactions linked to the SalesPitch item
 |  

Record types with an Interactions view
 

Each entry in the Interactions grid represents a single email, phone call, meeting, etc. For each Interaction, the grid displays the following information:

 

 | Title
 | The name of the Interaction. If the Interaction was created from an email or similar item, this will typically be the subject line.

 | Participants
 | The Contacts included in this Interaction, as well as their roles.

 | Date
 | The date the Interaction took place.

 | Type
 | The type of Interaction, such as an email blast or a phone call.

 | Status
 | 

If the Interaction was a DocuSign e-signature request, the current signing status is reflected here. Select the status to view the document in DocuSign.

 - Requires an active DocuSign integration. This column is not available on all tabs.

 | Created On
 | The date and time the Interaction was added to PensionPro.

Columns on the Interactions grid
 

 

 When I sort the Interactions grid by date, why doesn't it also sort by
 time?
 

 
 

 Timestamps are not available for all Interaction items. As such, PensionPro
 cannot guarantee that Interactions sharing the same date will be sorted
 by
 time in all circumstances.
 

 

 

 

Viewing Interaction Details

 

Double-click any entry in the Interactions grid to open it in a new Interaction tab.

 

 | General
 | Displays Interaction information, including Title, Date, and Details.

 | Participants
 | 

The names, emails, and roles of any Contacts associated with this Interaction.

 - Double-click a participant to open their Contact record.

Views for the Interactions tab
 

The Interaction's Details are included on the General view of the Interaction tab. If the Interaction was created from an email, the body of the email will be shown here; if added or edited manually, this will be the text that was entered during that time.

 

 

Editing Interactions

 

 Requires Security Rights: Add/Edit Interaction
 

 

If needed, an Interaction's information—such as its details, participants, or what record it's linked to—can be edited in a number of different ways:

 

 - All data for an Interaction can be quickly edited by hovering over it in the Interactions grid and selecting Edit on the right-hand side. - This option is not available on the Client tab.

 - Information on the General view of the Interaction tab can be updated by selecting Edit at the top-right.

 - Individuals on the Participants view of the Interaction tab can be managed by hovering over their entry and selecting Edit or Delete on the right-hand side. New participants can be added by selecting Add at the top-right of the grid.

 

 

 Note: Not all Interactions can be edited. If PensionPro
 generated the Interaction when sending a Blast Email or other item (such
 as a Secure File Exchange), editing its data is not possible.
 

 

 

 

Resending or Forwarding Blast Email Interactions

 

If an Interaction was originally sent via Blast Email, it can be sent to the recipient again using the original subject, body, and settings. To resend an Interaction:

 

 - In the Interactions grid, click to select the desired Interaction.

 - Select More > Resend Interaction.

 

Alternately, the Blast Email can be forwarded to a new recipient; this is useful if a Contact was missed when the Blast Email was originally sent. To forward an Interaction:

 

 - In the Interactions grid, click to select the desired Interaction.

 - Select More > Forward Interaction. The corresponding window displays. - This option is not available on the Client tab.

 - Use the To and CC fields to choose the new recipient(s).

 - (optional) Use the Forward Body to add additional text to the email. - The original email body will still be included; any Forward Body text will be inserted directly above it in the final email.

 - Select Send.

 

 

 Note: The ability to forward Interactions is only available
 on the Business tier.
 

 

 

 Note: A Blast Email Interaction that has been re-sent
 or forwarded will not include any of its original attachments. If an
 attachment is needed, a new Blast Email should be sent.
 

 

 

 

Deleting Interactions

 

 Requires Security Rights: Delete Interaction
 

 

Interactions can be deleted from the Interaction grid. To permanently remove an Interaction, hover over it and select Delete on the right-hand side. This option is not available on the Client tab.

 

 

Adding Interactions to PensionPro

 

New Interactions are added to PensionPro in one of three ways:

 

 - An Interaction is automatically generated when a Blast Email or Secure File Exchange is sent.

 - An email file can be dragged into the PensionPro window.

 - Interaction details can be entered by hand.

 

These methods are discussed in detail in the sections below.

 

 

Manually Adding an Interaction

 

 Requires Security Rights: Add/Edit Interaction
 

 

New Interactions can be recorded on the Interactions grid, or from any location in PensionPro via the Add Data menu. While this is typically the only method to add communications such as phone calls and in-person appointments, emails and other messages can be added this way as well.

 

To get started, use either of these methods to open the Add Interaction window:

 

 - On the Interactions view of either the Contact, Plan, Prospect, Opportunity, or Proposal tab, select Add at the top-right of the grid.

 - Navigate to Add Data > Interaction.

 

Then, use the Add Interaction window to complete these steps:

 

 - Select the Interaction's Type and enter a Title.

 - (optional) Enter any additional Details, such as what information was communicated.

 - Enter the Interaction Date that the communication took place.

 - One or more Participants fields will be shown based on the chosen Interaction Type. Use these fields to search for and select the appropriate Contacts. At least one participant is required.

 - (optional) If adding the Interaction from the Contact tab or the Add Data menu, use Link Type to choose the record type to link this Interaction, then use the [Record] Name field to search for and select the item to link. - Adding the Interaction from one of these record types (such as a Plan or Proposal) will link the Interaction by default; in this case, this field will not be available.

 - Select Save.

 

 

Adding an Interaction from an Email File (Drag-and-Drop)

 

 Requires Security Rights: Add/Edit Interaction
 

 

If communication with a contact occurred via email, that email can be quickly added as an Interaction by dragging it into PensionPro. When added in this way, PensionPro can fill in many of the Interaction details directly from the email so that the information doesn't need to be entered by hand.

 

 

 Note: This functionality is only available in Google
 Chrome and Microsoft Edge browsers.
 

 

 

 Note: The steps in this section assume the reader is
 using
 Microsoft Outlook for Windows. PensionPro does not provide support for
 other
 email applications or services. Outlook for Web is likewise not supported.
 

 

 

To add an Interaction from an email:

 

 - Drag the email from the Outlook inbox to the desktop or other location on the device. - Alternately, save the email as a .eml file using the steps provided in the Microsoft Support article Save an Outlook message as a .eml file, a PDF file, or as a draft↗.

 - Drag the saved file into the PensionPro window. The Add Interaction window displays.

 - Select the Interaction Type. - Only email-based Interaction Types will be available.

 - PensionPro fills the Title, Details, Interaction Date, and Participants from the email. Review and make changes if desired. - PensionPro will attempt to match email addresses to saved Contacts. If a match cannot be found, PensionPro will display a warning and the individual will not be added as a participant.

 - (optional) Use Link Type to choose the record type to link this Interaction, then use the [Record] Name field to search for and select the item to link. - If the email is added while an applicable record is open (such as a Plan or Proposal), PensionPro will assume the Interaction is associated with the record and fill these items accordingly.

 - Select Save.

 

 

 Note: Attachments included with the email will not be
 saved with the Interaction.
 

 

 

 

Automatically-Generated Interactions

 

Some PensionPro features that generate emails will create Interactions when used. For example, after a Blast Email is sent, a copy of the email will be stored as an Interaction. All applicable Contacts will be saved as participants, and records will be linked where appropriate (e.g., a Blast Email sent to Plan Contacts will be linked to the corresponding Plans).

 

 

 Note: Any associated attachments or files are not saved
 with
 the Interaction.
 

 

 

Features that create Interactions include (but are not limited to):

 

 - Annual Data Collection

 - Blast Email

 - DocuSign Integration

 - Dynamis Integration

 - Secure File Exchange

 

 

 Tip: The Interaction Type used for Blast Email Interactions
 can be set in
 Blast Email Preferences.
 

 

 

 

Customizing Interaction Types & Roles

 

 Requires Security Rights: Maintenance
 

 

PensionPro includes a selection of Interaction Types and Interaction Roles by default, but these can be customized to organize communications and participants as needed. Types and Roles are managed as List Values; refer to that article for more information.

 

To customize Interaction Types and Interaction Roles:

 

 - Navigate to Maintenance > List Values. The corresponding tab displays.

 - In the list of views, expand Core > expand Interaction and select either Interaction Role or Interaction Type.

 - Create a new entry by selecting Add and entering the required details, or edit an existing entry by hovering over it in the grid and selecting Edit on the right-hand side.

 

In addition to Display Name and Description, Interaction Type and Interaction Role entries have additional properties not present for other List Values. These properties are discussed in the below items.

 

Interaction Roles

 

Roles identify what part each participant played in an Interaction. These could be To, From, and CC if the Interaction was an email, or Organizer and Attendee if the Interaction was a meeting.

 

Each Interaction Role will need to be assigned a Base Role so that PensionPro understands how to correlate the Role with a participant. This is most relevant when dragging emails directly into PensionPro. For example, a meeting invite email added to PensionPro may use the email's To field to determine who the attendees were. In this case, Attendees is the Role listed on the Interaction, but To is the Base Role that sets its functionality.

 

Roles
Description

 | From, To
 | General-use roles

 | CC, BCC
 | Alternate recipients specific to email

 | Sender, Signer
 | Roles in digital e-signature collection

Base Roles for Interactions and what they represent
 

Interaction Types

 

Similarly to Interaction Roles, Interaction Types will require a Base Type that helps define and categorize it. For example, Inbound and Outbound Phone Calls could be added as separate Interaction Types, but they would both use the Call Base Type.

 

Each Interaction Type also requires at least one Role, which are the same Interaction Roles defined above. When a new Interaction is created, participants can only be added to Roles available for the given Interaction Type. Continuing the example we used earlier, a Phone Call might only use the From and To Roles, as CC is not a concept that applies to a telephone.

 

Type
Description
Roles

 | Call
 | Two-way phone call
 | From, To

 | E-Signature Document
 | File for signature via digital signing service
 | Sender, Signer, CC

 | Email
 | Standard electronic mail
 | From, To, CC, BCC

 | Fax
 | Transmission via fax machine
 | From, To, CC, BCC

 | Mail
 | Physical mail delivery
 | From, To

 | Meeting
 | In-person or virtual conference
 | Organizer, Attendee

 | Secure File Exchange
 | A secure file sent to or from PlanSponsorLink
 | From, To

Base Types for Interactions and recommended Roles

articles.title: Notes
articles.body: Gone are the days of putting a sticky note into a retirement plan's over-stuffed manila folder, but that doesn't mean those pieces of information should be lost. Notes are the digital equivalent to leaving a memo in a file; they are extra bits of information that do not easily fit into another area within PensionPro. Notes can be found in multiple locations in PensionPro, but they function the same no matter where they are located. Notes can also be bulk imported, marked as Important, or sorted into Note Categories for grouping and reporting.   Tier Availability: Track, Team, Business   Article Contents   - Working With Notes - Notes Categories - Bulk Import Notes - Adding Hyperlinks to Notes - Frequently Asked Questions     Working With Notes   Notes can be added to the following record types: Client, Plan, Contact, Project, Distribution, Opportunity, Proposal, and Prospect. Anywhere that Notes can be added, the Notes view will display with a number beside it to indicate how many Notes are present.   To access Notes, navigate to the associated record, then select the Notes view. The grid will display information about each Note, including values such as the Note text, Created On, and Created By. Hovering over a Note in the grid will display the Edit and Delete options on the right-hand side.   Note: The Delete Notes Security Right is required in order to delete Notes.   A new Note can be added by selecting Add at the top-right of the grid. During Note creation, enter the desired Note text; this acts as the message that displays in the Notes grid. Assigning a Note Category will aid in tracking and grouping of related Notes. Additionally, a Note can be optionally be marked as Important, which will flag it with the Important icon and can be used to sort and filter Notes containing critical content.   Notes can also be archived by selecting Archive when adding or editing a Note. As opposed to deleting a Note, archiving it retains a record of the Note's existence. By default, archiving a Note hides it from the Notes grid. Archived Notes can be shown or hidden from the Notes grid by selecting More > Show Archived/Hide Archived.     Note Categories   Note Categories allow users to group related Notes, such as General Notes or Billing Notes. These Note Categories can then be used to filter or group the Notes grid, to filter the relevant PensionPro Reports, or to create custom queries in PensionPro Fetch.    Note: Note Categories are maintained as List Values. More information on List Values can be found in the article List Values.     Bulk Import Notes   Two Power Tools are available that provide the capability to mass import Notes. These are:   - Client Notes Import Power Tool - Plan Notes Import Power Tool   For more information on importing Notes and Note Categories, refer to the article Data Import - Notes.     Adding Hyperlinks to Notes   Hyperlinks can be copy and pasted directly into Notes, or they can be shortened using HTML syntax. To do the latter, copy and paste the following formatting into a Note, and then replace "URL link" with the desired hyperlink and "Click here" with the display text.   Click here     Frequently Asked Questions   - I have all Rights, why can't I edit/delete a Note? The Note Editing Allowed and Allow Deletion of Notes preferences may be set to No. To enable editing/deletion of Notes at a global level, navigate to the Data Security view of PensionPro Preferences and set the values of these settings to Yes.

articles.title: PensionPro API
articles.body:
The PensionPro API is a powerful tool for working with PensionPro data outside of the application itself.  With a little bit of creativity and development know-how, firms can automate their processes, build their own tools, or integrate with third-party software. This article will discuss managing aspects of the API and assist firms in getting started with this functionality.

 

Tier Availability: Team, Business

 

 

 Warning: This article covers v2 of the API. Although v1
 is still in effect and can continue to be utilized, some functionalities—such
 as API key management—are not supported in the legacy version. v1 will be
 deprecated on May 31, 2026; for guidelines on converting, refer to the article
 Upgrading to API v2.
 

 

Article Contents

 

 - What To Know

 - 
API Key Management
 - Adding a New Key

 - Personally Identifying Information

 - Regenerating & Deleting Keys

 - Using the API Docs

 - 
Call Limits - Reducing "Too Many Request" Errors

 - 
Webhooks
 - Adding a Webhook

 - Webhook Format

 - Managing Webhooks

 

 

What To Know

 

The PensionPro API is a RESTful↗ API that communicates using JSON over HTTPS.

 

A list of available endpoints and data models can be found at api.pensionpro.com. This page also serves as an interface for testing and building calls.

 

Security is maintained via the use of API keys, which are controlled by the firm and must be passed with each API call to verify its legitimacy. These keys may be optionally be restricted from accessing records containing personally identifying information (PII). API keys can be revoked at any time. A valid PensionPro username must also be passed with the call; changes made to records via the API will be recorded to the Audit Log of the Employee who executed the request.

 

API calls are directed toward the firm's production database, which contains live data. Upon request, a sandbox account can be provisioned so that live data is not at risk while development occurs. To get started, please submit a Support request ticket to the PensionPro Help Desk.

 

 

API Key Management

 

 Requires Security Rights: Maintenance

 

 

 Note: The instructions in this section only apply to v2
 of the API. If using v1, refer to the Firm API Key section
 of the article
 Firms & Locations.
 

 

API keys are added and controlled within Firm & Location maintenance:

 

 - Navigate to Maintenance > Firms/Locations. A new Firm tab opens.

 - Select the API Access view from the list on the left.

 

The API Access grid contains any API keys that have already been generated, along with their descriptions and the dates the keys were last used to make a call. Hovering over an entry in the grid displays the Edit and Delete options on the right-hand side.

 

Above the grid, PensionPro displays the total number of API calls that have been made in the current cycle, providing a simple means of measuring usage against the monthly limit. For more information, refer to the section Call Limits.

 

 

Adding a New Key

 

 Requires Security Rights: Add/Edit API Access

 

To create a new API key:

 

 - Select Add at the top-right of the grid. The Add API Key window displays.

 - Note that the API Key field has generated a randomized 24-character key.
 - This character string cannot be edited.

 - 
The full key will be lost once the window is closed. Either utilize the key immediately upon creation, or copy the key to a safe location.

 - Create a Name for the key.

 - (optional) Select any PII Endpoints that the API key should be allowed to access. - Refer to the section Personally Identifying Information, below.

 - (optional) Add a Description. - For firms who generate many keys for fine control over their usage, the Description can be a crucial asset to keep API access organized.

 - To the right of the API Key field at the top of the window, select Copy to Clipboard. - To ensure that the generated key is not immediately lost, the new entry cannot be saved until this action is performed.

 - Select Save.

 

 

Personally Identifying Information

 

It is rarely good practice to give individuals full API access to areas of PensionPro containing PII when this information is not needed. This is especially true for firms that outsource API development to third parties. For this reason, API keys can be configured to only allow access to the data that is relevant for the task being performed. A 401 "Unauthorized" error will be returned if an API key is used in an attempt to retrieve or alter information it has not been permitted to access.

 

Data from the following categories will be restricted unless the API key has been configured to allow access; permissions for each category are added individually to allow for fine-tuning:

 

 - Distribution Information Details

 - Employees

 - Family Members

 - Files

 - Interactions

 - Notes

 - Participants

 - To-Dos

 

 

 Note: All endpoints not included in the above list do not
 contain PII and can be accessed without restriction by any API key.
 

 

 

Regenerating & Deleting Keys

 

 Requires Security Rights: Add/Edit API Access

 

In the event that an API key has been lost, potentially compromised, or is no longer needed, it can be deleted entirely or simply swapped out for a new key with all the same settings.

 

 

 Warning: An API key will cease to function as soon as it
 is regenerated or deleted. The key cannot be recovered.
 

 

To replace a current key with a new one while keeping the settings of the original, click to select the key within the grid, then select More > Regenerate API Key. A dialog asks to confirm this action; select Yes to continue. An updated API key will then be displayed in a new window; select Copy to Clipboard, then Save. As with adding a new API key, the full updated key will be lost when the window is closed.

 

Alternately, to remove a key, hover over it in the grid, then select Delete on the right-hand side.

 

 

Using the API Docs

 

The page at api.pensionpro.com provides a full list of endpoints and schemas for the PensionPro API, separated by category. Select an endpoint to view it in more detail; doing so will display the parameters that may be used in the call as well as the applicable data model.

 

 

 Note: Ensure that you are referencing the correct version
 of the API by using the dropdown at the top-right of the page.
 

 

The API Docs are also interactive, providing an environment for calls to be built and tested within a user interface. To get started:

 

 - Select the green Authorize button at the top-right of the tag list.

 - Enter a valid combination of full API key and username, separated by a pipe ( | ) character (in the format xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx|username), then select Authorize.

 - Expand the desired endpoint. At the top-right of the endpoint's entry—in the Parameters header— select Try it out.

 - Enter any parameters as appropriate, then select Execute. The API Docs will generate and submit the request with the given parameters; the reply from the server will be displayed below in the Responses section.

 

 

 Tip: The details of the request will be included along
 with the server response. If a test call is successful, it can be copied
 from the API Docs; this is a great way to ensure correct syntax during development.
 

 

 

Call Limits

 

To safeguard servers against negative performance issues associated with third-party API use, PensionPro imposes the following limits:

 

 - 100 requests per minute

 - 2,000,000 requests per month

 - 2 concurrent file uploads

 - 2 concurrent file downloads

 

The PensionPro servers will return status code 429 "Too Many Requests" in the event one of these limits is exceeded; further requests will be likewise rejected until the appropriate amount of time has elapsed.

 

The monthly request limit can be tracked via the counter above the API Access grid within Firm & Location maintenance. The requests-per-minute limit is reported in the x-ratelimit-limit and x-ratelimit-remaining headers of every server response.

 

The next section provides suggestions for lowering the number of API requests to avoid reaching the call limits listed above. However, if optimized code is insufficient to resolve errors caused by these restrictions, PensionPro can provide a High Volume add-on for $295 /month. This add-on increases the call limits to 300 requests per minute and 5,000,000 requests per month. To upgrade, please submit a Support request ticket to the PensionPro Help Desk.

 

 

Reducing "Too Many Request" Errors

 

The simplest method of avoiding call limit restrictions is to reduce the number of requests that are made to PensionPro's servers. Consider investigating the following options:

 

 - Optimize code to eliminate calls that aren't being used, and identify areas where multiple requests to the same endpoint could be condensed into a single call.

 - Use Expand parameters on parent items to retrieve data from linked children, as opposed to querying the children individually by parent ID.

 - Implement caching solutions such as web/DOM storage↗, or save temporary information to a local file or database.

 - Utilize Webhooks as opposed to polling PensionPro for updates.

 

If the number of requests being made are regularly exceeding the minute-by-minute limit and resulting in failed calls, it may be worth including a process in the code that regulates the rate of requests so that they are more evenly distributed over time. This type of throttling could be accomplished statically (execute the call every X seconds) or dynamically (if nearing the rate limit, delay the request).

 

 

 Will batching calls reduce the number of API calls? How about making parallel
 calls?
 

 
 

 No, batching calls or making calls in parallel will not reduce the number of requests made to the server.
 

 

 

Webhooks

 

 Requires Security Rights: Maintenance

 

In some situations, no action needs to be taken until a change is made within PensionPro. While it is possible to make regular calls to the PensionPro servers and check for updated data, it can be more efficient to establish a webhook instead. Implementing a webhook means that PensionPro will transmit details of the change after it happens, making it unnecessary to repeatedly poll for new information.

 

A webhook can notify of additions, updates, and deletions affecting the following endpoints:

 

 - Client

 - Contact

 - EmployeePlanLink

 - Plan

 - Project

 - Task

 

Webhooks are added and managed within Firm & Location maintenance:

 

 - Navigate to Maintenance > Firms/Locations. A new Firm tab opens.

 - Select the Webooks view from the list on the left.

 

If a webhook has already been established, it will be displayed within the Webhooks grid. Hovering over the entry in the grid displays the Edit and Delete options on the right-hand side. Select Refresh to manually update the grid.

 

 

Adding a Webhook

 

 

 Note: Only one webhook may be established at a time. A new
 webhook cannot be added until the prior one is removed.
 

 

To create a new webhook:

 

 - Select Add at the top-right of the grid. The Add Webhooks window displays.

 - Enter the URL that will receive the webhook requests.

 - Select at least one Endpoint to receive updates for. - There is no limit to the number of Endpoints that may be selected, but it is good practice to only add the Endpoints that are required for the code to function.

 - Select Save.

 

A request will immediately be sent to the provided URL to verify that it is a valid target. If the request fails, PensionPro will display an error, and a new URL will need to be provided before the webhook can be added.

 

 

Webhook Format

 

Below is an example webhook request sent from the PensionPro API. This webhook, which uses the Plan endpoint, would have been generated after a Plan's name was updated.

 

{
 "Data": {
 "DisplayName": "New Plan Name",
 "AuditedOn": "2025-01-31T18:39:02.5958734Z",
 "CreatedByFullName": "First||Last",
 "RecordId": 123456,
 "EventType": "Update Record",
 "EntityType": "Plan",
 "CreatedById": 12345
 }
}
 

EntityType values are available for query through the API at /v2/auditLogs/entityTypes.

EventTypes: Add Record, Update Record, Delete Record.

 

 

Managing Webhooks

 

Any changes made in PensionPro that affect the data within any of the established endpoints will be queued as a POST request; queued requests will be transmitted to the receiving URL in 5-minute intervals. A log of sent requests can be obtained by clicking to select the webhook in the grid, then selecting More > Export Request Log. This log includes the request date/time, the entity type that triggered the request, and the response from the receiving URL.

 

After the webhook is created, a Shared Key will be provided in the grid. This key is transmitted in the header of webhook requests, making it possible to confirm that the request was sent from PensionPro.

 

The State of the webhook will also be included in the grid. In the event the webhook receives an error response from the receiving URL, State will display Error and no further requests will be sent. Errors can be reviewed by exporting the Request Log as detailed above. Once the issue is resolved, click to select the webhook in the grid, then select More > Reactivate to return the webhook to an Active State so that it may resume sending requests.

articles.title: PensionPro Marketplace
articles.body:
Thanks to its influence throughout the TPA industry, PensionPro is able to act as a "gateway" to other applications that build onto what PensionPro already offers. To assist users in discovering ways to further evolve the way they work, the PensionPro Marketplace contains information on innovative partner solutions that integrate with PensionPro, and offers a means of quickly and easily getting in touch with these companies.

 

Tier Availability: Track, Team, Business

 

Article Contents

 

 - Accessing the Marketplace

 - Exploring Products

 

 

Accessing the Marketplace

 

The Marketplace can be opened from any screen in PensionPro. To do so, select Marketplace from the Navigation Panel on the left-hand side of the application.

 

 

Exploring Products

 

When opened, the Marketplace tab displays brief descriptions of each of our partner products. Select Learn More underneath any product to view more details about the product and the partner company offering it.

 

If interested in a product, select View Website to be taken directly to the partner's website for further information.

 

PensionPro also provides the option to reach out directly to our partners. Select Contact under any product to display the Contact Partner window. Here, PensionPro will generate a simple message for the partner company; this message can be edited prior to sending if desired. When satisfied, select Contact in this window to send the message; it will be delivered directly to the partner, who will reach out in response to the request. Additionally, an Interaction will be saved to the Contact tab of the Employee who sent the request.

articles.title: Recording & Tracking Time
articles.body:
When Employees track their work time in PensionPro, firms are able to evaluate the time spent on plan activity and client interactions, as opposed to other non-client-facing duties. By understanding how to enter Time Slips and learning how to use the Time Tracking feature efficiently, managers and users alike can evaluate and streamline their workflow using built-in reports, making their operations more efficient.

 

Tier Availability: Team, Business

 

Article Contents

 

 - 
Setting Up Time Tracking
 - Adding Time Codes

 - Adding Billing Codes

 - Time Tracking Preferences

 - 
Adding Time Entries
 - Linking Time Slips to a Plan

 - Automatically Calculating Time Worked

 - Using the Time Dashboard

 - Marking Time as Reviewed for Billing

 - Time Reports

 

 

Setting Up Time Tracking

 

Firms looking to implement Time Tracking for the first time should follow the items in this section, which will cover creating the appropriate List Values and enabling optional firm-wide settings.

 

 

Adding Time Codes

 

 Requires Security Rights: Maintenance

 

First, Time Codes will need to be defined for the firm. Time Codes represent the various activities that an Employee can be engaged in throughout their day—from performing various administrative activities to quality review and client outreach. These can also include non-billable time, such as for meetings, breaks, and training. These codes are often broken into categories of related activities for ease of use.

 

To add a new Time Code:

 

 - Navigate to Maintenance > Time Codes. The Time Codes grid opens in a new tab.

 - Select Add at the top-right of the grid. The Add Time Code window displays.

 - Enter the Name and a Description.
 - The Name will be the code that Employees will see when adding Time Slips.

 - The Description will be shown alongside the code when adding a Time Slip, and should indicate what activity this Time Code is used for.

 - (optional) Select a Billing Code.
 - If used, Billing Codes must be established prior to adding the Time Code. Refer to the next section, Adding Billing Codes.

 - A Billing Code can be used with as many Time Codes as needed.

 - If the activity represented by this Time Code should be charged to clients, select Billable.

 - Select Save.

 

 

Adding Billing Codes

 

 Requires Security Rights: Maintenance

 

Each Time Code can optionally be assigned a Billing Code, which will help correlate the Time Code to an appropriate charge when using an external billing software. These codes are added to PensionPro as List Values, and should match any codes used by the firm's existing billing practices.

 

To add a new Billing Code:

 

 - Navigate to Maintenance > List Values. The List Values grid opens in a new tab.

 - In the Views list on the left, expand the Core > General categories, then select the Billing Code view. The corresponding grid displays.

 - Select Add at the top-right of the grid. The Add Billing Time Code window displays.

 - Enter the Display Name and Description.

 - Select Save.

 

 

Time Tracking Preferences

 

 Requires Security Rights: Maintenance

 

PensionPro includes a number of firm-level preferences to customize the behavior of the Time Tracking feature for all Employees. The below views can be found within Maintenance > Preferences > PensionPro.

 

General

 

 - 
Include Completed Projects on Time Entry: Allows users adding a Time Slip to link it to a Project that was previously completed.

 - 
Show Timeslip Prompt: When a user completes a Project Task, a dialog will ask if they entered a Time Slip for that activity. If the user selects No, the Task does not complete, and they have the opportunity to submit the Time Slip before continuing.

 

Data Security

 

The following preferences extend the functionality provided by the Add/Edit Other Employee Timeslips Security Right:

 

 - 
Allow Deletion of Other Employees' Timeslips: Users with the above Security Right can delete Time Slips linked to other Employees.

 - 
Allow Editing of Other Employees' Timeslips: Users with the above Security Right can edit Time Slips linked to other Employees.

 

 

Adding Time Entries

 

To add a new Time Slip and record time worked:

 

 - Select Add at the top-right of the Time Dashboard. The Add Time Slip window displays. - Alternately, use the Time option found in the PensionPro header on every page.

 - Select a Time Code based on the type of work performed.

 - Enter the Time Worked and Work Date.

 - (optional) Add a detailed Description of the work performed.

 - (optional) Link the Time Slip to a Plan.

 - (optional) Determine if the time worked is Billable to a client.

 - Select Save.

 

 

 Note: Users with the Add/Edit Others Timeslips
 Security Right can also edit the Assigned To field to
 add
 this Time Slip on behalf of another Employee.
 

 

 

 

Linking Time Slips to a Plan

 

Time Slips can optionally be linked to a specific Plan, Plan Cycle, Project, and even a specific Task. This can help clearly identify what the performed work was servicing.

 

When completing the Add Time Slip window, use the Plan field to search for and select the Plan to link the Time Slip to. Once a Plan is selected, additional fields for Project, Task Grouping, Task, and Plan Cycle will be displayed.

 

If a Project tab or Plan Cycle tab is open, using the Time option found in the tab header—to the far right of the Project or Plan Cycle name—will display the Add Time Slip window like usual, but will also automatically complete the Plan, Project, Task Grouping, Task, Plan Cycle, and/or Time Code fields based on what information is currently in focus.

 

 

Automatically Calculating Time Worked

 

When Employees fall into the rhythm of adding Time Slips following each activity performed throughout the day, PensionPro can speed up the process by automatically calculating the amount of time that was worked. This can help users avoid the necessity of manually tracking start/end times for tasks and mentally converting them into an amount.

 

At the bottom of the Add Time Slip window, PensionPro displays the following information:

 

 - 
Start Time: The beginning of the workday

 - 
Elapsed Time: The time that has passed since the Start Time

 - 
Today's Time: The amount of time that has been accounted for in today's Time Slips

 - 
Remaining Time: Any Elapsed Time that has not yet been accounted for

 

Each user can set their own Start Time by typing it into the field, or using the icon on the right to select a time. The remaining fields will adjust appropriately based on the Start Time.

 

To the right of the Time Worked field is a Set Time Worked option. This will populate the Time Worked with the Remaining Time value. This means that if Time Slips have been added regularly throughout the day, the Time Worked field will be populated with the exact amount of time that has elapsed since the last Time Slip was entered.

 

 

Using the Time Dashboard

 

The Time Dashboard offers a centralized location for viewing, adding, and editing Time Slips. Here, Time Slips can be reviewed regardless of whether they were created today, last week, or six months ago.

 

To access the Time Dashboard, navigate to Dashboards > Time. By default, the grid displays any Time Slips that have been entered for today's date. Hovering over an item in the grid displays the Edit and Delete options on the right-hand side.

 

Although the Time Dashboard initially shows Time Slips that match today's date, other time periods can be chosen using the Time Entries dropdown above the grid. Some built-in options are available—such as Yesterday, This Week, and Last Week—or Custom Day and Custom Range may be selected to help fine-tune results. Custom Date Ranges may not exceed 60 days.

 

Users with the Add/Edit Other Employees Security Right can use the Employees dropdown above the grid to view and manage Time Slips on behalf of another Employee.

 

 

 Why can't I edit or delete this particular Time Slip? Others work fine.
 

 
 

 The Time Slip in question has likely been Reviewed for Billing, in which
 case it can no longer be edited.
 

 

 

 

Marking Time as Reviewed for Billing

 

 Requires Security Rights: Access Power Tools

 

One of the primary benefits to recording time worked is to make sure that all time spent on behalf of a client was billed correctly. In PensionPro a Time Slip can be marked as Reviewed for Billing to indicate it has been properly accounted for, which can be reflected in select reports. Doing so also prevents any further edits from being made to the Time Slip.

 

Time Slips are marked via the Time For Billing Power Tool, located under Power Tools > Billing > Time For Billing. This allows batches of Time Slips to be marked at the same time. Use the below instructions to assist in completing the Power Tool.

 

Step 1: Options

 

This step contains a single item, which determines whether the Power Tool should mark or unmark Time Slips as billed. Set this option as desired, then select Next.

 

Steps 2 & 3: Filters & Selections

 

In Step 2, add any extra columns to be included in the grid in Step 3, and add any filters to reduce the resulting dataset. A useful column here is Work Date, which can then be used as a filter to only return Time Slips entered for a set period of time—say, a week or a billing cycle. For a more in-depth explanation of this process, refer to the article Column Selections & Filters. Select Next to continue.

 

Step 3 will return the Time Slips matching the criteria set in Step 2. Select any Time Slips to apply the changes to, then select Next to continue.

 

Steps 4 & 5: Review & Finish

 

The Review step shows a summary of the changes that will be made; select Execute to complete the Power Tool. The changes will be applied immediately, and a summary of the results will be displayed on the Finish step.

 

 

Time Reports

 

 Requires Security Rights: Management

 

PensionPro includes a number of built-in reporting options for viewing and exporting data based on entered Time Slips. These reports can be accessed by navigating to the Reporting > Management Reports > Time Reports category. For more details about each report available here, refer to the Time Reports section of the article PensionPro Reports.

articles.title: To-Dos
articles.body:
"Follow up with this client." "Check this figure." "Send this letter." We all need the occasional reminder to make sure something gets done, especially if it's not part of our usual routine. To-Dos can be created from anywhere in PensionPro—and linked to a relevant Contact, Plan, and more—to make sure nothing slips through the cracks. No more sticky notes on the monitor.

 

Tier Availability: Team, Business

 

 

 Note: Some items may not be available in all tiers.
 

 

Article Contents

 

 - Overview

 - 
Viewing To-Dos
 - To-Dos Dashboard

 - To-Dos On Other Tabs

 - Reporting on To-Dos

 - 
Creating To-Dos
 - Adding a Single To-Do

 - Adding Multiple To-Dos via Power Tools

 - 
Working With To-Dos
 - Moving To-Dos

 - Completing To-Dos

 - To-Do Notes

 - Frequently Asked Questions

 

 

Overview

 

A To-Do is used to track an item of work that needs performed. For Business tier users, this may be a rarely-occurring or unexpected obligation that falls outside the scope of a Project; for those on PensionPro's Team tier, To-Dos will be the primary method of tracking administrative tasks.

 

Each To-Do is assigned to an Employee, who is responsible for completing it. All of an Employee's To-Dos can be found in the To-Dos Dashboard.

 

Sometimes, a To-Do will exist independently, simply being an item that needs fulfilled. Other times, it might be linked to one of many PensionPro record types, to indicate that it is a To-Do item for that record—such as a To-Do for a particular Plan or Project. To-Dos can be linked to the following record types:

 

 - Contact

 - Opportunity

 - Plan

 - Project

 - Proposal

 - Prospect

 

Linking a To-Do to one of the above records is another method of tracking the work that was performed for it, and all linked To-Dos can be viewed within the record itself.

 

 

Viewing To-Dos

 

Any To-Do can be found on the To-Dos Dashboard or via built-in reporting. To-Dos linked to other record types can also be viewed within the linked record.

 

 

To-Dos Dashboard

 

By default, the To-Dos Dashboard displays any incomplete To-Dos assigned to the user. To access this Dashboard, navigate to Dashboards > To-Dos. Double-click on any To-Do in the Dashboard grid to open it in a new tab.

 

Hover over a To-Do in the grid to display the Edit and Delete options on the right-hand side.

 

Although completed To-Dos are hidden from the Dashboard to prevent clutter, they can be displayed at any time by selecting More > Show Completed.

 

Employees with the View Other Dashboards Security Right can use the Assigned dropdowns above the grid to view the To-Dos assigned to any other Employee (or All Employees at once), as well as viewing the To-Dos assigned by an Employee to another Employee.

 

More information on Dashboard functionality can be found in the articles Dashboard Basics and Customizing Dashboard Views.

 

 

To-Dos On Other Tabs

 

As outlined in the Overview section of this article, some record types—such as Plans and Projects—can be linked to To-Dos. To view all of the To-Dos linked to a record, first navigate to the record by opening it in a new tab, and then select To-Dos from the list of views on the left side of the tab. The corresponding grid displays each To-Do for the record, regardless of who it is assigned to or its completion state.

 

Double-click on any To-Do in the grid to open it in a new tab; alternately, hover over a To-Do to display the Edit and Delete options on the right-hand side.

 

 

Reporting on To-Dos

 

The To-Do List report is available to retrieve a list of To-Dos customized by creation date, priority, Employee, status, and/or associated record. To access this report, navigate to Reporting > To-Dos > To-Do List.

 

For more information on using the built-in reporting functionality, refer to the article PensionPro Reports.

 

 

Creating To-Dos

 

A To-Do can be created individually as a one-off item, or can be added to multiple Plans at once using Power Tools.

 

 

Adding a Single To-Do

 

A new To-Do can be added from one of three places:

 

 - The Navigation Panel, by selecting Add Data > To-Do

 - The To-Dos Dashboard, by selecting Add at the top-right of the grid

 - The To-Dos view on an appropriate record type, by selecting Add at the top-right of the grid

 

Regardless of the method used, the Add To-Do window will display. To create the To-Do:

 

 - Give the To-Do a Name and (optional) Description.

 - (optional) Set a Started On date and Due Date.

 - (optional) Set a Status and Priority. - The available options for Status are determined by List Values, located under Core > General > To-Do Status.

 - 
Assigned To will contain the user's name by default; if desired, use this field to search for and select a different Employee to assign the To-Do to.

 - (optional) If linking the To-Do to a specific record, use Link To Type to select the appropriate record type; then, use the record name field to search for and select the record in question. - Any To-Dos added directly from a record will automatically be linked to that record.

 - Select Save.

 

 

Adding Multiple To-Dos via Power Tools

 

 Requires Security Rights: Access Power Tools

 

The To-Do Power Tool can be used to simplify the process of creating multiple similar To-Dos for any number of Plans.

 

 

 Note: When finished, the To-Do Power Tool will add and link
 one To-Do to each chosen Plan. Power Tools cannot be used to add and link
 To-Dos to any other record type.
 

 

To use the Power Tool:

 

 - Navigate to Power Tools > To-Dos. The To-Do Power Tool opens at Step 1.

 - Enter the desired Title, Description, Due Date, etc. for Items 1-5 following the criteria in the section Adding a Single To-Do.

 - For Item 6, select either Assigned To Employee Plan Role or Assigned To Employee. - Each of the To-Dos created by this Power Tool can be assigned to the same Employee; alternately, they can be assigned to different Employees based on each Plan's designated Employee Plan Roles.

 - If Employee Plan Role was chosen in the previous step, select the Role in Item 7. If Employee was selected, search for and select the appropriate Employee instead.

 - Select Next.

 - In Steps 2 and 3, apply filters as necessary, and select the desired Plans. Refer to the article Column Selections & Filters for more detailed instructions.

 - Review the changes to be applied in Step 4, then select Execute.

 

Upon completion of the Power Tool, the To-Do will be added to all Plans selected in Step 3.

 

 

Working With To-Dos

 

An in-progress To-Do can be reassigned to a different Employee or linked to a different record. The To-Do can then be marked as completed when its directions have been fulfilled.

 

The following sections should be used within the Edit To-Do window. To open this window:

 

 - Locate the To-Do in the To-Dos Dashboard or appropriate view grid; alternately, open the To-Do in a new tab.

 - Hover over the To-Do in the grid and select Edit on the right-hand side. Or, on the To-Do tab, select Edit at the top-right of the grid instead.

 

 

 Note: The Edit Other To-Dos Security Right
 is required to edit a To-Do currently assigned to another Employee.
 

 

 

Moving To-Dos
